introduction_markdown: Answer ALL FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. Begin each question on a new page. Give labelled diagrams where these will make the answers clearer. You are advised to read carefully through the question paper before you begin your answers. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Duration: Two hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In a tabular form state one source and one effect of the following pollutants:

(i) Carbon monoxide

(ii) Dust

(iii) Nitrogen dioxide

(iv) Oil spills

(v) Fertilizers *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Pollutant | One source | One effect |
|---|---|---|
| (i) Carbon monoxide | Incomplete combustion of fuels in vehicle engines (exhaust fumes), burning of wood or charcoal | Combines with haemoglobin to form **carboxyhaemoglobin**, which **reduces oxygen transport** in the blood, causing headaches, dizziness and even death |
| (ii) Dust | Quarries, cement factories, construction sites, bush burning, unpaved roads | Causes **respiratory diseases** (coughing, asthma); it also settles on leaves and **reduces photosynthesis** |
| (iii) Nitrogen dioxide | Vehicle exhaust, burning of fossil fuels in industries and power stations | Dissolves in rain to form **acid rain**, which damages plants, buildings and lakes; it also irritates the lungs |
| (iv) Oil spills | Leaks from oil tankers, offshore drilling platforms and pipelines | Form a film on water that **cuts off oxygen and light**, **killing fish, plants and sea birds** |
| (v) Fertilizers | **Run-off** (leaching) of excess artificial fertilizers from farmland into rivers and lakes | Cause **eutrophication**: algae grow rapidly, die and are decomposed by bacteria, which use up the oxygen, so **fish die** |

questions.enonce_markdown: How does energy flow in an ecosystem? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Energy flows through an ecosystem in **one direction** along food chains:

1. The **Sun** is the source of energy. **Producers** (green plants) trap a small part of the light energy by **photosynthesis** and store it as chemical energy in organic compounds.
2. This energy passes to **primary consumers** (herbivores) when they eat the plants, then to **secondary consumers** and **tertiary consumers** (carnivores) when they feed on each other. Example: grass $\rightarrow$ grasshopper $\rightarrow$ frog $\rightarrow$ snake.
3. At each **trophic level**, a large part of the energy (about **90 %**) is **lost** as **heat** in **respiration**, in movement, and in the uneaten or undigested parts (faeces, bones). Only about **10 %** is passed on to the next level, which is why food chains are short and the numbers or biomass decrease along the chain.
4. When plants and animals die, **decomposers** (bacteria and fungi) feed on the dead remains and release the remaining energy as heat.
5. Energy is **not recycled**: it leaves the ecosystem as heat, so the ecosystem needs a constant supply of energy from the Sun.

questions.enonce_markdown: How does carbon circulate in nature? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Carbon circulates in the **carbon cycle**:

1. The atmosphere contains carbon in the form of **carbon dioxide** (about 0.04 %).
2. **Green plants** remove carbon dioxide from the air by **photosynthesis** and make **carbohydrates, proteins and fats** (organic carbon compounds).
3. Carbon passes to **animals** when they **feed** on the plants (and on other animals) along the food chain.
4. Carbon dioxide returns to the atmosphere by the **respiration** of plants, animals and microorganisms.
5. When plants and animals **die**, **decomposers** (bacteria and fungi) break down their remains and release carbon dioxide by respiration (decay).
6. **Combustion** of wood and of **fossil fuels** (coal, petroleum, gas, formed long ago from buried dead organisms) and **volcanic activity** also release carbon dioxide into the air.
7. Carbon dioxide dissolves in the **oceans and rivers**, where it is used by aquatic plants and algae and forms carbonates (shells, limestone).

The cycle keeps the amount of carbon dioxide in the air nearly constant, although burning fossil fuels and deforestation tend to increase it.
